correctness.rationale: The BFS distance formula gives an invariant decomposition into 5(r-1) leaf-bundle contrasts, four nonconstant Fourier blocks and one zero-mass constant mode. The constant-mode equation r(2*4^p-2^p-2*3^p)=2^p has a unique p>1. Exact rational interval inequalities at 9/7 and a proved exponential Descartes sign-variation lemma keep both nonconstant blocks negative at the root, uniformly in all r>=2. Strictness below follows from Li-Weston; the global witness is positive above. The unique kernel yields exact affine embedding dimensions; Taylor inversion proves the asymptotics. The attached code independently reconstructs distances with BFS and tests complete finite spectra, with no claim of exhaustive finite-to-infinite certification.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general implicit finite matrix criterion does not directly imply the explicit all-r threshold, its mode dominance for every r, its kernel or asymptotic. Clique coronas have all core-core distances one, while C5 has distance-two core pairs. One-point bouquets identify vertices rather than giving each cycle vertex private leaves. Hence these stronger-looking results do not cover the claimed family.

originality.rationale: The closest full text proves only the bare C5 threshold and general finite-matrix procedure (Sanchez), or studies distorted negative type on bipartite and Hamming spaces (Robertson). Related formulas for clique coronas, five-cycle bouquets, and weighted cycles concern different metric objects and do not imply the all-multiplicity pentagonal corona formula. The uniform global-versus-Fourier obstruction proof, equality line and asymptotic have not been located in checked sources. Historical alias risk remains.
residual_risks: A historically older result under the aliases generalized roundness, pentagonal corona, thorn graph or sunlet extension could have the same uniform formula but may not be indexed.
Primary literature outside the accessible search subset was not exhaustively surveyed; novelty is best-knowledge, not independently certified.

value.rationale: The object is a natural sequence of unicyclic graph metrics formed by uniformly thickening the private-leaf boundary of the smallest nontrivial odd cycle. The result determines a sharp isometric Hilbert-snowflake invariant for all leaf multiplicities, proves that a global mass-imbalance obstruction overtakes the preexisting C5 Fourier obstruction, classifies the unique equality direction, and obtains a nonzero explicit two-term asymptotic. This is an exact family classification, not an isolated numerical value or a mere parameter substitution.
